question: An analyst must validate a Claude-written competitor comparison, produced with web search on, before it informs a pricing meeting tomorrow. Which sequence is correct?
options: A) Open the source behind each claim and read it, then look up any unsourced claim independently, then mark whatever is still unconfirmed, then list the claims the decision rests on.
B) Look up every claim independently, then list the claims the decision rests on, then open the sources behind them, then mark whatever is still unconfirmed.
C) Mark whatever is still unconfirmed, then open the source behind each claim and read it, then list the claims the decision rests on, then look up unsourced claims independently.
D) List the claims the decision rests on, then open the source behind each one and read it, then look up any unsourced claim independently, then mark whatever is still unconfirmed.
correct_answers: D) List the claims the decision rests on, then open the source behind each one and read it, then look up any unsourced claim independently, then mark whatever is still unconfirmed.
explanations: Reading every cited source before deciding which claims matter treats all claims as equally important, and working out what the decision rests on last makes that step unable to guide any of the work.

Independent lookup of everything before any prioritisation spends the analyst's limited time evenly across claims that matter and claims that do not, and it ignores the sources already attached to the answer.
Marking unconfirmed material before any checking has happened is meaningless, and identifying the decision-critical claims is left until the third step, after the effort has already been spent.

Correct. Scope the check to the decision-critical claims, review the cited sources for those first because the original content shows whether anything was misread, then fill the gaps independently and flag what remains unconfirmed.
